item.title: Buckeyes HC Ryan Day Reports Massive Update On Their QB’s Injury and It’s Not Good News
item.description: In the final minutes of a tense road win over Indiana, Ohio State Buckeyes ‘ season shifted in an instant. A single hit in the fourth quarter left the Buckeyes’ starting quarterback on the sideline with his throwing arm in a sling. It was unclear for how long Julian sayin will remain out of the games, but now head coach Ryan Day has news and it is not very leasing for the Ohio State. Ohio HC Ryan Day reports QB’s injury update Ohio State’s 2026 season took a major turn on October 17 when starting quarterback Julian Sayin suffered a significant injury to his throwing arm during a hard-fought 19-15 road victory over Indiana. Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) leaves the field in a sling following the 19-15 win over the Indiana Hoosiers in the NCAA football game at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. Julian Sayin entered 2026 as one of the more accomplished young quarterbacks in the country. After transferring from the Alabama portal and developing behind the scenes, he took over as Ohio State’s starter in 2025 as a redshirt freshman. That season he threw for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns with a nation-leading completion percentage near 77%, finished fourth in Heisman Trophy voting, and earned Big Ten Freshman of the Year honors. With just over eight minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game, Sayin dropped back on first-and-10 near the Indiana 38-yard line. Indiana defensive lineman Mario Landino beat the edge protection and sacked him. The hit pinned Sayin’s right (throwing) arm against his body in an awkward position as he tried to throw. Sayin went to the ground wincing, was evaluated on the field by medical staff, and was unable to grip the football normally. He left for the locker room and later returned to the sideline with his right arm in a sling. He did not re-enter the game. Immediately after the game, Ryan Day said Sayin would “probably be out for several weeks.” On the Monday following the game, Day reiterated that the absence would be at least several weeks while medical testing continued, and he declined to speculate further. The tone shifted significantly on Tuesday, October 20, after practice. “Based on the nature of the injury, we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season and then also him not being available for the postseason.” Day said . “We’re not going to put any timeline on his recovery, but he is out indefinitely. If he’s not able to return this fall, then we’re putting a plan together for that as well. That’s the update I have right now,” he added. As of October 21, 2026, there is still no official timeline or detailed medical update beyond Day’s comments. But Day confirmed his “indefinite” unavailability means he will remain out for this season. item.description: The Houston Texans have released rookie linebacker Aiden Fisher , their seventh-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. He is set to join the Kansas City Chiefs’ practice squad. NFL insiders reported the move on October 20, citing Fisher’s All-American season at Indiana. Houston released him after three appearances. Chiefs add rookie LB to practice squad after Texans move The Kansas City Chiefs are signing Fisher to their practice squad, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, as they remain unbeaten after winning every game this season . He signed with Houston on May 12. His release came as the team adjusted its roster for players returning from injuries. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers haven’t had much go right so far this season, currently sitting at 1-5 after a recent home loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in overtime. The Whites sit seventh after seven league matches, collecting 10 points from two wins, four draws and one defeat. They have scored nine goals and conceded six, giving Farke reason to feel encouraged by his side’s defensive organisation. However, Leeds suffered a 6-3 defeat against Chelsea in the EFL Cup third round, exposing the demands of competing across multiple competitions. Dominic Calvert-Lewin has established himself as the first-choice centre-forward, leaving limited opportunities for his fellow senior striker. Leeds need sufficient cover for injuries, suspensions and demanding fixture schedules, particularly if they intend to maintain their early league position. Their recruitment plans could determine how effectively Farke manages that challenge during the winter window. Leeds United consider January exit for 27-year-old striker According to an exclusive report by Football Insider journalist Pete O’Rourke , Leeds United are prepared to sell Lukas Nmecha in January, provided they secure a replacement first. The 27-year-old German joined Leeds from Wolfsburg as a free agent in 2025 and has struggled to secure regular minutes behind Calvert-Lewin. His contract expires in June 2027, while negotiations over an extension have stalled. Nmecha has made seven appearances across all competitions this season, recording two assists without scoring in 224 minutes, according to Opta Analyst. His mobility, experience in German football and ability to operate centrally offer useful depth. However, his limited involvement raises questions about whether he can deliver consistently when handed extended opportunities. Several Bundesliga clubs, including FC Köln, reportedly hold interest in the forward. January would allow foreign clubs to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with him. Leeds have identified Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul as a potential solution. The 26-year-old Frenchman scored 20 Ligue 1 goals last season and has already registered seven in his opening seven league matches this term. His recent senior France caps prove his growing reputation, although competition from Everton and other Premier League clubs could complicate negotiations. Should Farke risk losing Nmecha before securing a replacement? LEEDS, ENGLAND – AUGUST 08: Lukas Nmecha of Leeds United looks on during the during the pre-season friendly match between Leeds United and RB Leipzig at Elland Road on August 08, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Leeds should prioritise recruitment before approving Nmecha’s departure. His contract situation creates financial pressure, but selling their only natural alternative to Calvert-Lewin without another striker would leave Farke exposed during a demanding campaign. Lepaul offers an attractive profile, having recent scoring form with experience in French football. His 27 league goals mean that he could compete for minutes immediately. However, Leeds must assess his pressing, physical suitability and ability to adapt to Premier League defenders before committing substantial funds. The club should negotiate a replacement deal first, then pursue a sale at a reasonable fee. If Rennes demand an unrealistic January premium, retaining Nmecha until summer may represent the safer option. Losing him for nothing would hurt financially, but sacrificing attacking depth could cost Leeds valuable league points.

item.title: Como humiliate Manchester United, Michael Carrick's job on the line
item.description: Como humiliate Manchester United, Michael Carrick's job on the line A footballing lesson. Alongside the clash between LOSC and Galatasaray, another hugely important match took place this Wednesday at 18:45. Como hosted a Manchester United side in crisis, who headed into the match winless in six consecutive games across all competitions (three draws and three defeats). The result: the crisis deepens, as Como humiliated Manchester United 4-1. The Italians quite simply delivered a masterclass, outclassing a woeful United side technically and tactically. On Wednesday night, United looked to have given up on their manager, Michael Carrick. Nico Paz (with a brace), Anastasios Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon scored for the Italian revelation, who claimed their second win in three Champions League matches. As for Manchester United, the Red Devils' last win in any competition dates back to September 10, on the opening matchday of the Champions League against Sabah. This humiliation away to a club making their Champions League debut this season further weakens Carrick's position, even raising doubts over whether he will be in the United dugout for this weekend's Premier League fixture! item.title: “Didn’t Know C-Tier Players Would Qualify for WNBA Finals MVP”: Angel Reese Fans Poke Fun at Candace Parker Over Latest Endorsement Amid Dream Star’s Red-Hot Run
item.description: Angel Reese © X/@WNBA Candace Parker had to eat her words this season about Angel Reese’s impact. The former WNBA player has been an Indiana Fever fan, considering she hosts her YouTube show with Aliyah Boston. Though Parker had not been very impressed with Reese’s last few seasons, the Atlanta Dream star has exceeded expectations this season. And fans on social media won’t let the three-time WNBA champion forget that. While ranking players in 2025, Parker kept Reese among Tier-C players. And now, when the player-turned-analyst was asked who could win the 2026 WNBA Finals MVP, her answer included the center. View on Threads Reese’s fans didn’t miss the chance to highlight her earlier remarks, though she recently admitted she was wrong about Reese. One wrote: “I didn’t know C-tier players would qualify for wnba finals mvp” View on Threads View on Threads View on Threads View on Threads View on Threads The Dream and the Golden State Valkyries are tied 1-1 after two games, as Reese led the team to a 79-65 win in Game 2. She scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, along with one steal and two blocks. The team now heads back to Atlanta for Game 3 on home court. The finals series has seen defensive power play from both sides. Angel Reese came with a mission in Game 2 The Valkyries contained the Dream well in Game 1 and managed to edge them out 68-64. Reese could score just 14 points in the first half and was completely silent in the second. However, she came prepared for the next game. After the Game 2 win, Reese said: “I let my team down last game, not really contributing as much as I could in the second half. I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark. And I think I did that.” Allisha Gray is still feeling the impact of her finger injury and hasn’t shown the same impact in the first two games. Reese will have to take the challenge and propel the team to the other side. Given her Game 2 performance, she seems to be ready for it. item.title: Why Yankees fans who wanted change won't like Hal Steinbrenner's plans
item.description: NEW YORK - Two weeks after their playoff elimination, Yankees brass finally offered a public assessment of another season without a championship. But nothing said by owner Hal Steinbrenner, GM Brian Cashman or manager Aaron Boone will satisfy a fan base still waiting for a title since 2009, and wondering why a sharp change of direction isn't coming. Cashman has agreed to a new deal, and Boone returns for his 10th season, the final year under his guaranteed contract, without promise of an extension. After a long public silence, what you got from ownership was lament about a lack of offense, but no proclamations, no directives, no or-else statements. Nothing about fundamentally altering the culture of a 93-win regular-season team that, once more, failed to defeat an equal or better postseason opponent. By now, Yankees Universe probably wasn't anticipating much more, but it's no less disappointing. "We had a lot of bumps and bruises along the way, but the team was fantastic - it was a world championship-caliber team," Steinbrenner said Wednesday, following a second straight AL Division Series elimination by an AL East foe. "That’s absolutely what we expect," Steinbrenner said of the "mission'' to win it all. "That is always our goal, which is why we put so much effort and resources into the roster every offseason to field a team that can accomplish that. "And I certainly felt we had that team this year. It just didn’t pan out." Fallout of Aaron Judge's 'all-in' roster comments Beyond a rightfully agitated fanbase, pointed criticism of the Yanks' discipline, culture and approach was aired by bold-faced names such as CC Sabathia, Anthony Rizzo and Alex Rodriguez. Right after the Yanks were swept by the Rays in the AL Division Series, captain Aaron Judge - sidelined with a calf injury during postseason - mused on the front office's "all-in" strategy to build a championship team. While saying he hadn't listened to Judge's entire post-Game 3 comments, Steinbrenner was "not upset" by the captain's quotes. "If I was a player, I’d have expectations that my ownership group would do everything in their power every offseason to field a team that can win a championship,'' said Steinbrenner, believing "we went all-in this season." On Tuesday, Steinbrenner and Judge "had a great conversation over a number of subjects as we always do," related to the team's direction. "We’ve got some decisions that need to be made right after the World Series is over," including whether to extend free-agent qualifying offers to closer David Bednar and second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., and Judge is "going to be a part of all that." Without going into detail, Cashman said he's spoken with some of those critical of the organization's recent run. "We're always open-minded," said Cashman, adding that "we're always trying to find higher ground" toward a winning culture. "Right or wrong, I think this organization is progressive." item.title: Travis Kelce Leaves Chiefs Rookie Mansoor Delane Starstruck Over His ‘Aura’ in Mic’d Up Moment
item.description: Mansoor Delane (left); Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs. Credit: David Eulitt/Getty; Carmen Mandato/Getty NEED TO KNOW Mansoor Delane was starstruck by Kelce while watching him play from the sidelines during the Chiefs-Chargers game on Sunday, Oct. 18 The Chiefs rookie was in awe of the tight end veteran’s 14-yard reception Kansas City extended its winning streak to five games with its victory over the Los Angeles Chargers Mansoor Delane is learning from the best. The Kansas City Chiefs rookie, 22, offered an unfiltered reaction to teammate Travis Kelce ’s performance at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18, when the team defeated the Los Angeles Chargers , 22-6, to extend its win streak to 5-0. Delane, the Chiefs’ sixth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, was mic’d up when he reacted to Kelce, 37, hauling in a 24-yard pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes . Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs. Credit: Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty “Kelce has so much aura,” the first-year cornerback said of the three-time Super Bowl champion in an Instagram clip while watching the play happen in real time. “He got so much aura, bro. Kelce has so much aura, like if I had a son, I want him to be just like [Kelce].” Mahomes completed a short pass to the Chiefs tight end, who rumbled down the field, rolling down at the Chargers’ 20-yard line for a 24-yard gain. The Arrowhead Stadium fans went wild, including Kelce’s wife, Taylor Swift , who hugged singer Este Haim while celebrating the play. item.title: Former NFL QB Calls for Kansas City Chiefs to Trade for Young 3x 1,000-Yard Receiver
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Even before the 2026 NFL season kicked off, analysts thought the Kansas City Chiefs had a weakness at the receiver position. Now that breakout performer Tyquan Thornton has suffered a fractured ankle and will be on injured reserve for the foreseeable future, the Chiefs’ already thin group of pass-catchers needs even more help. Technically, the Chiefs have until the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline to decide whether to swing for the fences, solve the problem from within, or turn to free agency for someone like Tyreek Hill. For now, they’re being urged to trade for a 26-year-old star that not many others are talking about ahead of the trade deadline. Related: 5 NFL Trades That Could Happen Before Week 7 Russell Wilson Wants Kansas City Chiefs to Trade for Garrett Wilson Oct 18, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (5) runs with the ball after a catch in the first quarter against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Teams seeking a receiver upgrade have been linked to the usual suspects such as Brian Thomas Jr., Jerry Jeudy, or Jauan Jennings. Yet, if none of those names move the needle, how about a 26-year-old receiver who’s recorded a 1,000-yard season three times? That would be Garrett Wilson of the New York Jets, who enter Week 7 with a 2-4 record. Recently, former NFL QB Russell Wilson took to “ Set Hut ” with Chris Long to explain why he wants to see the Chiefs step up and trade for the Jets’ former first-round pick who’s under contract through 2030. “If I’m the Kansas City Chiefs… who would I go get? I’m gonna get Garrett Wilson. If the Jets keep losing, I’m gonna go get Garrett Wilson because I believe that Garrett Wilson, down the field, with his ability, he’s a smart guy, he learns quickly, he’d be great in the Andy Reid style offense. Patrick Mahomes and him, how he gets in and out of his breaks. They haven’t had a receiver like him. If I’m the Kansas City Chiefs, I’m watching Garrett Wilson.” Russell Wilson on Kansas City Chiefs Trading for Garrett Wilson Garrett Wilson to Chiefs? @DangeRussWilson thinks the Chiefs should trade for Garrett Wilson https://t.co/PRHRrVVLpq — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 20, 2026 There have been no indications that the Jets are ready to trade a player they just signed to a four-year, $130 million contract extension last July. Yet, first-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr. is coming off the first 100-yard game of his career, and they also spent a first-round pick on tight end Kenyon Sadiq. In other words, the Jets would still have a pair of young pass-catchers they believe in, plus Adonai Mitchell. As a result, it’s possible an offer too good to refuse could pry Wilson out of New York and into the welcoming arms of Kansas City, where he’d get to catch passes from Patrick Mahomes. item.title: KC Chiefs Report Brings New & Affordable Receiver Target Before NFL Trade Deadline
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With the Kansas City Chiefs reportedly shopping on the trade block for a pass catcher to boost their wide receiver corps, the team has been linked to a one-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl champ as a logical target soon. After a very disappointing 6-11 finish to their 2025 campaign, the Chiefs are back to being Super Bowl contenders in 2026. Heading into a Week 7 Sunday night matchup against the Seattle Seahawks , Kansas City is one of the last undefeated teams left in the NFL. While their defense has been rock solid and their run game — led by early MVP contender Kenneth Walker III — has been fantastic, they could use more weapons in their passing attack. Especially after Tyquan Thornton suffered a likely season-ending injury three weeks ago and Rashee Rice battling leg injuries. The Chiefs have been linked to a variety of notable receiver targets in recent weeks, including Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jerry Jeudy. There has even been talk of a reunion with team great Tyreek Hill in free agency. Should Kansas City Chiefs target Chris Godwin Jr. trade? Oct 8, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. (14) makes a catch past Dallas Cowboys linebacker Shemar James (50) at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Well, an NFL executive told Jason La Canfora this week that “ Even if they sign Hill, Andy Reid) is going to want to do something else ” to boost their WR corps. And the insider believes that should be Tampa Bay Buccaneers veteran Chris Godwin Jr. “How much of (Godwin’s) decline is due to the fact the Bucs haven’t been able to push the ball downfield for years and Baker Mayfield was not good or healthy least year and same thing this year?” La Canfora wrote. “And the loss of Mike Evans has set Tampa’s pass game back. “The Chiefs likely need more than one roll of the dice at the receiver position given all their issues there, and lack of another playmaker was a concern even before the season began.” The 10-year veteran has battled injuries for the last few seasons, and that should make him an affordable option in a trade. When healthy, he is a four-time 1,000-plus yard receiver and one-time Pro Bowler. If the Chiefs added him and Hill for the second half, they would be a big boost to their receiver corps. item.title: ‘They don’t have that with Luka’: Lakers star explains why fans will take to Luka Dončić more than LeBron James
item.description: Feb 10, 2025; Los Angeles, CA; Los Angeles Lakers stars Luka Doncic and LeBron James. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers are officially in the Luka Dončić era after superstar forward LeBron James departed for the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency over the offseason. Now, Dončić is embracing being the primary face of the franchise, something he hasn’t been since his days with the Dallas Mavericks. “I think it’s just very important to me to do a lot of connection with the fans,” Dončić told the California Post . “Before every game at home, I sign things and I take pictures. When we go on the road, I take pictures. I think for me, it’s giving back to the fans the way they supported me. The way they care for me. It’s very important to give back to them.” It took some time for Dončić to adjust after being traded from Dallas, where he thought he’d spend his entire career, but he finally feels at home on the West Coast. “After that, at training camp last year, I felt I was where I belonged,” Dončić said. “I feel very good in LA. I’m very excited. Very happy. Obviously it’s a beautiful place to live. But just being with the Lakers organization, being a part of it, it’s such an honor. It’s amazing to be here.” Dončić’s star teammate, Austin Reaves, even believes that Lakers fans will take to Dončić more than they were able to with James, and explained why. “I think with the Bron situation it was a little different just because Bron and Kobe were battling for the best player in the NBA for multiple years, so Lakers fans at the time probably hated LeBron,” Reaves said. “Not that they didn’t accept him when he was here, but they still probably had the ‘Kobe is better’ type of mentality. But they don’t have that with Luka. He was kind of after Kobe. They don’t have a reason not to embrace him like a Kobe or someone else who was a Laker legend.” The post ‘They don’t have that with Luka’: Lakers star explains why fans will take to Luka Dončić more than LeBron James appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Kramarić’s Hoffenheim status under pressure ahead of Lyon clash
item.description: Kramarić’s Hoffenheim status under pressure ahead of Lyon clash Kramaric’s season has yet to get going. After undergoing groin surgery following the World Cup, the Hoffenheim record goalscorer missed almost the entire pre-season and has struggled to regain match fitness. Across eight appearances this campaign, he has accumulated just 179 minutes on the pitch. The Croatian started for the first time this season in Hoffenheim’s 3-2 defeat against Besiktas last week, playing 70 minutes before returning to the bench for the subsequent league defeat against Hamburg. He was introduced in the 63rd minute in that game and also remained among the substitutes for Sunday’s 2-1 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach. Ilzer recognises Kramaric’s quality and experience but insists that every player must earn their minutes. “You can’t give away playing time as a coach. Players simply have to earn their minutes through performances,” the Austrian explained. He also acknowledged that players returning from injuries need time to build up their fitness and form, making communication with them particularly important. Few players at Hoffenheim can match Kramaric’s standing at the club. He has scored 158 goals in more than a decade with the Bundesliga side and netted 15 times last season. Sporting director Andreas Schicker described him as a club legend when his contract was extended in May. Despite his reduced role, Kramaric has not publicly voiced his frustration . The forward, who finished as a World Cup runner-up with Croatia in 2018 and third in 2022, has largely kept his thoughts to himself in recent weeks. Hoffenheim’s 2-1 victory in Gladbach offered some relief after a difficult spell, but tougher tests lie ahead. Thursday’s Europa League encounter with Lyon, who lead Ligue 1, will be followed by a Bundesliga meeting with Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday. For Kramaric, both fixtures offer an opportunity to work his way back into Ilzer’s plans.

Coming out of their Week 6 bye, the 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals are last in the AFC North, but they have a real chance of making a move towards the top of the division as the year rolls along. One of the main reasons why this Bengals team is different is thanks to their much-improved defense. Specifically, the Bengals' defensive line is playing great to start the season. However, one key name isn't really a part of the turnaround. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler revealed that Shemar Stewart, thanks to his lack of involvement in the Bengals' edge rusher rotation, is a legitimate "surprise" name to watch on the trade market this Fall. Shemar Stewart tabbed as a 'surprise' trade candidate for Bengals "One surprise name a few teams are tracking is Cincinnati edge rusher Shemar Stewart," Fowler writes. "... Cincinnati typically doesn't move its young draft picks, but it would be surprising if the Bengals haven't received inquiries on Stewart, whose upside remains high." The Bengals could be getting trade calls on Stewart this season, and Fowler believes he's a legitimate trade candidate for the 2026 NFL trade deadline. A huge reason why is that, through the first part of the season, Stewart has barely played. He has 17 snaps on defense, well below Cedric Johnson, the team's fourth edge rusher. With the Bengals losing Trey Hendrickson, it was natural to assume Stewart would see an increase in playing time. But the 2025 first-round pick has fallen by the wayside on defense this season. With rookie second-rounder Cashius Howell impressing so far in an increasing role, the Bengals would, at best, have Stewart as their fourth edge rusher. While the Bengals won't cut ties with Stewart for nothing, especially not so early into his second NFL season as a first-rounder, the Bengals might actually entertain trade offers. item.title: FIA Deploys Major F1 Cost Cap Rule Change to Add More Complexity Amid Resistance
item.description: The FIA has stepped in with major changes under the Cost Cap to restrict F1 teams from taking advantage of a loophole. It came to light that the Formula 1 teams were trying to game the Cost Cap regulations by utilizing employees for F1 activities but not adding their wages under the Cost Cap, and keeping them on the payroll while showcasing their work in non-F1 activities. Some examples of this relate to engineers sharing office space with employees undertaking non-F1 activities; some also worked from off-beat areas like the canteens or well-being places within the office compound. Several F1 teams also have separate divisions, like Red Bull Advanced Technology, McLaren Applied Science and Aston Martin Performance Technology, with Mercedes and Ferrari also undertaking out-of-F1 activities using F1 technology. Changes Under Which Section (Photo by Joe Portlock/Getty Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610110383 // Usage for editorial use only // To curb this loophole being utilized by some F1 teams, the FIA has stepped in with a 12-page regulation under Section F (Operational) that reads ‘Article F6: Physical and IT segregation between F1 activities and non-F1 activities’. The IT side has been heavy on such practice, and so the FIA has restricted movement of employees from one office space to another – any such move will require cards that register and track the movements of F1 employees and non-F1 workforce. As such, they are segregated and accounted for. The FIA has the liberty to verify and cross-check at times to see if the F1 teams are following the rules in place. The restriction extends even to communication services that may pass information. Creation of Certain Areas The FIA wants the F1 teams to create ‘Restricted F1 Area’, ‘Restricted Non-F1 Area’, ‘Restricted Shared Area’ and ‘Non-Restricted Shared Area’, to better manage and segregate all the employees, not just physically but also via communication tools. The shared area will have another undertaking of ‘Approved Operational Support Personnel’, for better accountability. The transfer of employees from one department to another will also require a cooling-off period, especially between F1 and non-F1 workforce, while there is a natural cool-off period for employees changing companies. (Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610110384 // Usage for editorial use only // Near Draconian Rule Change The regulation will come into effect on January 1, 2027; failing to adhere will result in a Cost Cap breach, and a penalty will be applied, which could be financial or even points deductions from the F1 championship. The huge, almost draconian set of changes from the FIA has resulted in resistance from F1 teams, who are finding certain aspects of the Cost Cap already complicated. This adds to the complication further, as the layers keep on adding.

Sir Henry Cecil’s extraordinary training career Sir Henry Cecil was one of British horse racing’s most successful and admired trainers. Born in Aberdeen on January 11, 1943, he established his training career in Newmarket. And became a dominant force in Flat racing for more than four decades. Cecil first took out his own training licence in 1969. His breakthrough at the highest level came with Bolkonski, who won the 2,000 Guineas in 1975. Followed by Wollow’s victory in the same Classic a year later. His success continued through the 1980s and 1990s, when his Warren Place stable became synonymous with elite racehorses. Sir Henry Cecil achievements included: 10 champion trainer titles in Britain. 25 British Classic victories, including four Epsom Derby winners. Four St Leger winners and eight Epsom Oaks winners. His victories included the 2,000 Guineas, the St James’s Palace Stakes, the Sussex Stakes on two occasions, the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes and the Champion Stakes (watch below). He retired in October 2012 with an unbeaten record and was widely celebrated as the world’s leading racehorse. Sir Henry Cecil died on June 11, 2013, aged 70, after a long battle with stomach cancer. He had been diagnosed with the disease in 2006 and continued to train horses while undergoing treatment. Although his health deteriorated during his final years, he remained involved in racing and witnessed Frankel’s extraordinary rise to international fame. Frankel’s final victory in the 2012 Champion Stakes at Ascot was particularly poignant. Cecil was there to celebrate the unbeaten champion in front of the crowd, including Queen Elizabeth II, and famously described Frankel as the best horse he had ever trained or seen. Cecil died less than eight months later, leaving behind one of the greatest records in British racing. His death prompted tributes from across the sport, with many remembering not only his achievements but also his horsemanship, personality and determination to return to the top. The forthcoming Unbeaten biopic will revisit that final chapter: the story of a trainer fighting personal adversity and a remarkable racehorse whose flawless career helped cement his place in sporting history. item.title: Four things we learned as Carrick runs out of excuses after Man United’s 4-1 humiliation in Italy
item.description: Four things we learned as Carrick runs out of excuses after Man United’s 4-1 humiliation in Italy Como welcomed Manchester United to their home, Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, where the two clubs opened a new European rivalry. United, currently enduring a six-game winless run and one of their poorest starts to a season in recent memory, would have seen this fixture as the ideal platform to turn their form around. Unfortunately, that was not the case. The Red Devils were thoroughly schooled in Italy, as Como thrashed them 4-1 (Joshua Zirkzee scoring for United). There was plenty to take away from the contest, and here are the key lessons we learned: Man United need to do the basics well Manchester United must rediscover the basics to reclaim their competitive edge. They struggle to win the ball back, often left chasing shadows. At times Bruno Fernandes showed a clear desire to press, yet his teammates have other ideas, leaving the side unable to execute a coordinated press (the only way it truly works). item.title: Liverpool star proves his point, drops incredible statement
item.description: Liverpool star proves his point, drops incredible statement One Liverpool star dropped an incredible statement on Tuesday evening. He has more than proven his point. Liverpool beat Villarreal on Tuesday evening and it was an interesting game. The Reds fell behind 2-0 and were genuinely awful in the first-half, but somehow rallied to go into the break level. That was primarily because Andoni Iraola made some tactical tweaks to solidify the midfield. A midfield that looked unbearably porous across the first half. Liverpool got back into the game, though, and the second half allowed for one player to make an incredible statement. No one should be under any illusions as to how good he truly is. Florian Wirtz's statement The match was ultimately a perfect example of what Florian Wirtz brings to this Liverpool team. The German didn't play in the first half but came on at half-time - the stark difference in the Reds' performance was clear for all to see. Of course, Wirtz simply getting on the ball and then scoring a goal is a simple way to see how he made an impact. He finished in the top 10 for passes made in the match, a ridiculous figure given he only played half of it. But the real statement was less in Wirtz's direct impact and more what it meant for the team. In that first half, Liverpool had 55 per cent of the ball. That translated to eight shots on goal for a mere 0.19xG from open play and a paltry 14 touches in the opposition box. That latter figure was as many as Villarreal managed on the counter-attack with less possession. Then on came Wirtz. Liverpool's possession dropped in the second period to 51 per cent but they did far, far more with the ball. Their shot count jumped to 14 for 1.5xG from open play. Above all, they got the ball into better areas - 14 touches in the opposition box skyrocketed to 30. This all came from Wirtz nitting things together. His 56 touches in one half blew everyone else out of the water. Ryan Gravenberch, for comparison, had 57 across the full 90 minutes and he had played Wirtz's position in the first half . It was as display that showed why Wirtz is vital to Liverpool. Without him, very little happens and the Reds are dependent on set-pieces to find a path to goal. With him? They can actually break teams down and all get involved in attacks.

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
